title: Prenatal Exposure to Select Phthalates and Phenols and Associations with Fetal and Placental Weight among Male Births in the EDEN Cohort (France).
ehr_evidence: Placental and birth weight were obtained at birth from hospital maternity records. Phenol and phthalate metabolite urinary concentrations were assessed in spot urine samples collected during pregnancy.
summary: Prospective birth cohort study examining associations between prenatal urinary concentrations of phenols and phthalates and placental weight, birth weight, and placental-to-birth weight ratio among 473 male births in France.
key_findings: Sum of parabens positively associated with placental weight (b = 7.12 g, 95% CI: 0.41, 13.9).
Benzophenone-3 positively associated with placental weight (b = 4.76 g, 95% CI: -1.77, 11.3).
Triclosan negatively associated with placental weight (b = -4.11 g, 95% CI: -8.26, 0.05).
MCNP negatively associated with placental weight (b = -10.9 g, 95% CI: -21.8, 0.09).
Benzophenone-3 positively associated with birth weight (b = 21.0 g, 95% CI: -3.45, 45.5).
MCOP and MCNP negatively associated with PFR (MCOP: b = -0.23, 95% CI: -0.58, 0.11; MCNP: b = -0.20, 95% CI: -0.54, 0.13).
No associations remained significant after FDR correction in sensitivity analyses (lowest corrected p-value = 0.39).
captured_features: Urinary phenol and phthalate metabolite concentrations
population: 473 mother-son pairs from the EDEN cohort in France, recruited before 24 weeks gestation
exposure_domain: Prenatal exposure to phenols and phthalates
limitations: Single spot urine sample leading to potential exposure misclassification
Missing placental weight data requiring inverse probability weighting
Restricted to male births limiting generalizability to females
Lack of detailed placental characteristics (e.g., thickness, vascularization)
Potential for chance findings despite penalized regression
